meta.title: Oh-a-Synth: a polysynth inspired by the 80s
meta.description: A 6-voice polysynth inspired by the classic sounds of the 80s. Play it free in your browser, no download. AU/VST3 plugin and Mac app on the way.

hero.h1: A polysynth inspired by the 80s, playable right now.
hero.positioning: Oh-a-Synth is a 6-voice polysynth inspired by the classic sounds of the 80s. Its real engine runs in this page. Pick a patch, sweep the filter, punch the chorus in. Power it on and play.
hero.powerHint: Click to power on. Silent until you do.

promise.heading: Why I built this
promise.body: I love the polysynths of the 80s. They're still all over records because they do a few things perfectly: rock-solid oscillators against a warm filter, and a chorus that turns one voice into a wall. Every software version I tried got the panel right and the feel wrong. So I built one that chases the feel, down to the small differences between voices that make six voices sound like six voices.

features.label: DCO
features.what: One digitally-exact oscillator per voice: polyBLEP saw, pulse with manual or LFO-swept width, a square sub one octave down, and a noise source shared across all voices, as on the hardware.
features.why: That era's character is solid pitch against a moving filter. Tuning never drifts here; the voice-to-voice tolerances live in the filter and amp instead, where the real chips had them.
features.mediaAlt: The DCO section of the Oh-a-Synth panel with PWM SRC switched to LFO, above an oscilloscope showing the pulse wave the engine is playing, its width moving.

features.label: VCF + HPF
features.what: A 24 dB/oct zero-delay-feedback ladder filter that self-oscillates near the top of the RES range and tracks the keyboard via KYBD. In front of it sits the 4-position HPF. Position 0 is the famous low-shelf bass boost.
features.why: Sweep FREQ on a held chord and there is no zipper, no stair-stepping: slider moves are smoothed per-sample inside the audio thread.
features.mediaAlt: The HPF and VCF sections with RES pushed high, above the filter's response: a resonant peak at the cutoff, FREQ 5.9, RES 8.3.

features.label: CHORUS
features.what: Two latching buttons, I and II; press both for I+II. A BBD-style stereo chorus modeled on the MN3009 bucket brigades: one delay line, two taps modulated in antiphase, wet path band-limited to 9 kHz.
features.why: This is the effect the era is remembered for. I is slow and lush, II runs faster, and I+II is the quick shallow warble the LESLIE ORGAN patch is built on.
features.mediaAlt: The CHORUS section with buttons I and II both lit, above a stereo goniometer showing the chorus spreading one chord across left and right.

features.label: ARPEGGIO
features.what: UP, UP&DN, or DOWN across 1, 2, or 3 octaves. Free-running from 0.5 to 20 Hz, or hit SYNC and the RATE slider snaps to twelve note divisions from 1/1 to 1/64, dotted values included. HOLD latches the chord.
features.why: Synced, it locks to your DAW's playhead in the plugin and to MIDI beat clock everywhere else, realigned every beat so it cannot drift.
features.mediaAlt: The ARPEGGIO section with ON, HOLD and SYNC lit, UP&DN and a two-octave range, synced at 1/16 and 128 BPM, above the keys the arpeggiator is playing.

features.label: PATCHES
features.what: Nine factory patches, from FAT BASS to WARM PAD. Save and name your own, and export or import them as flat .ohasynth.json files. In the app and plugin, favourite a patch ♥ and it gets its own section at the top of the selector.
features.why: The same file loads in the browser, the Mac app, and the plugin. A patch sketched on a laptop opens in Logic unchanged.
features.mediaAlt: The whole Oh-a-Synth panel with BRASS 1 just picked from the patch menu, above the factory patches with BRASS 1 lit.

features.label: MIDI
features.what: Notes with velocity, pitch bend with separate DCO and VCF depths, mod-wheel vibrato, sustain pedal, and 24-ppqn beat clock for the arp. The status readout names what's connected and what isn't.
features.why: Those machines ignored velocity entirely. The VEL slider maps it gently to level; set it to zero for that behavior.
features.mediaAlt: The BENDER pushed to the right, with its DCO and VCF depth sliders, above a chord held on the keyboard.

demo.heading: Hear it in a track
demo.body: Sixty seconds of dark synthwave where every sound is Oh-a-Synth, drums included. Each part is its own instance of the synth, starting from a factory patch.
demo.caption: The kick is the VCF, self-oscillating, pinged by the envelope. The snare and hats are noise through the HPF.

offer.heading: Get it
offer.webBody: Free and immediate. The synth at the top of this page runs the real engine, not a demo loop. Patches, filter and chorus are live here. The whole panel is in the app.
offer.desktopBody: The same instrument as an AU/VST3 plugin and standalone app for macOS. Every parameter is automatable. Patches are shared with the browser version. Builds are done. Distribution is waiting on Apple Developer ID signing and notarization.
offer.desktopCta: Tell me when the full version ships

rows.label: Polyphony
rows.value: 6 voices, with voice stealing (releasing voices stolen first)

rows.label: Oscillator
rows.value: 1 DCO per voice: polyBLEP saw + pulse (manual/LFO PWM), square sub −1 octave, shared noise; 16′/8′/4′ range

rows.label: Filter
rows.value: 24 dB/oct zero-delay-feedback ladder, self-oscillating; env (±, up to 9 oct), LFO (±3 oct), key follow to 105%

rows.label: High-pass
rows.value: 4-position HPF; position 0 is a low-shelf bass boost

rows.label: Envelope
rows.value: 1 ADSR shared by VCF and VCA, RC-style exponential segments; VCA env or gate mode

rows.label: LFO
rows.value: Triangle, 0.1–30 Hz, 0–2.5 s delay with fade-in, LFO TRIG override; routes to pitch, PWM, VCF

rows.label: Effects
rows.value: BBD-style stereo chorus: I (0.513 Hz), II (0.863 Hz), I+II (9.75 Hz)

rows.label: Arpeggiator
rows.value: UP / UP&DN / DOWN, 1–3 octaves, HOLD; free 0.5–20 Hz or synced (12 divisions, 1/1–1/64 incl. dotted); tempo from DAW transport (plugin), MIDI clock, or BPM 40–300

rows.label: Browser version
rows.value: Free. AudioWorklet DSP, ~3–12 ms latency. Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari. Web MIDI is unavailable in Safari

rows.label: Plugin & app
rows.value: AU, VST3, and standalone. macOS 11+, universal binary (Apple Silicon + Intel). All parameters host-automatable, state saved with the project

rows.label: MIDI
rows.value: Notes with velocity, 14-bit pitch bend, mod wheel (CC1), sustain (CC64), all-notes-off (CC120/123), 24-ppqn beat clock

rows.label: Patches
rows.value: 9 factory + unlimited user patches; flat .ohasynth.json, interchangeable across browser, app, and plugin

items.q: Does the browser version sound like the plugin?
items.a: Yes. The JavaScript and C++ engines are kept line-for-line equivalent: same oscillators, same filter, same chorus constants, same factory patches. Only the plumbing differs. The browser adds a few milliseconds of latency and runs at your audio device's rate.

items.q: Will it work in my DAW?
items.a: On macOS, yes: AU for Logic, VST3 for everything else. Every panel parameter is host-automatable, the current patch saves with your project, and you can run as many instances as you like.
The desktop version is macOS-only today. The browser version runs anywhere Chrome, Edge, or Firefox runs. If a Windows build happens, the notify list hears about it first.

items.q: Why can't I download it yet?
items.a: The app and plugins build and run today, but shipping them properly requires Apple Developer ID signing and notarization, which is in progress. The notify list gets the download link the day it's live.
By choice. The machines this draws on ignored velocity entirely; here the VEL slider maps velocity gently onto level. Set it to zero for the period-correct response.

items.q: Do patches transfer between the browser and the plugin?
items.a: Yes. A patch is a flat .ohasynth.json file, identical in both directions. Anything a patch doesn't name falls back to its default, so older patches keep loading as parameters are added.

ctaRepeat.heading: The synth is at the top of this page.
ctaRepeat.body: No download, no signup. Power it on and play it now.
